line: I was down bad, ain’t have a dollar to my name (Straight up) I was down bad, just my family and my gang (Straight up)
vault_lines: I was down bad, ain't have a dollar to my name (Straight up)
meaning:
The term “down bad” is a more simplified version of being desperate, which can apply to practically anything that a person could want. It was first coined within the late 2010s, and was made popular in Drake’s Laugh Now, Cry Later, featuring Lil Durk.

21 reminisces about his past life in the streets of Zone 6 ward of Atlanta where he never had any financial wealth, but only the company of his remaining family and his gang whom he struggled alongside with during certain points of his life, prior to becoming the rapper that he’s well-known as today, such as the loss of his best friend, as well as himself being shot 6 times at the age of 21.

line: Let them niggas split the drum, both of them get fifty

meaning: A drum is a high-capacity magazine for firearms. It usually holds up to 100 bullets. Rounded in shape (similar to a drum). This means both of his enemy’s get shot 50 times.
